Subject: Renewal questions: SLA and support options

Hi Naomi,

Our renewal for Redwood (contract #CS-10294) comes up Aug 15 and the exec team is asking for a straightforward path to a premium support package. High-level asks: 
- Move to a 24/7 priority support tier with a named on-call rotation and 15-minute P1 response SLA.
- Replace current latency target with a p99 end-to-end latency SLO of <= 150ms for our gen endpoints at 512 tokens.
- Reserve additional capacity (we expect up to 2x current committed throughput during product launches).

Can you send the pricing delta and a draft SLA addendum we can circulate internally? We can share our QPS and token distribution if that helps sizing.

Also looping in procurement (procurement@cloudscale.com) and Rahul for term/commit questions.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Director of Product
CloudScale Inc.

On Mon, Jul 15, 2028 at 09:12 AM Emma Li <emma@cloudscale.com> wrote:
> Our renewal for Redwood (contract #CS-10294) comes up Aug 15 and the exec team is asking for a straightforward path to a premium support package. High-level asks: 
> - Move to a 24/7 priority support tier with a named on-call rotation and 15-minute P1 response SLA.
> - Replace current latency target with a p99 end-to-end latency SLO of <= 150ms for our gen endpoints at 512 tokens.
> - Reserve additional capacity (we expect up to 2x current committed throughput during product launches).

Thanks for the details — quick technical read: 
- We can support a p99 ~120–150ms for typical gen workloads at 512 tokens if we reserve a Dedicated pool with consistent instance sizing (NVIDIA H100 class or equivalent). Achieving 120ms reliably depends on persistent prefix caching and a warm KV cache strategy.
- For capacity, a 2x reserved buffer is workable; we'll propose burst capacity (on-demand) plus a staged capacity reservation to avoid cold starts during launches.
- 15-minute P1 response is an ops policy, which we can offer at the premium tier; sustained uptime/latency commitments should be tied to a runbook and pre-deployment load tests.

I'll attach a recommended config and expected token cost delta. If you can share typical sequence lengths and distribution of short vs. long responses (1–128 tokens vs. 128–512 vs. 512+), I can finalize numbers.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — summary & next steps below.

Summary of what Redwood can commit for the renewal window: 
- Support tier: Premium / Priority 24x7 with named escalation roster and 15-minute initial response for P1 incidents. Detailed runbook and on-call roster to be attached to the SLA addendum.
- Latency SLO: p99 <= 150ms for gen endpoints at 512 tokens. We can include a service-level credit schedule tied to observed p99 over a monthly measurement window. Marcus will include a configuration appendix outlining required Dedicated pool sizing, cache strategy, and a proposed load-test plan.
- Capacity: Option A (18-month term): 1.5x committed base with discounted rate on additional burst capacity. Option B (24-month term): 2x committed base with a deeper commit discount (details in attached pricing table).
- Migration support: Redwood will provide a three-month migration uplift (credits that cover 2x capacity during the first three weeks of a major launch) to reduce risk of cold starts and throttling during the migration window.

Attachments included: SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf (draft addendum you can share with legal), Renewal_Reqs_CloudScale.xlsx (from Emma), CloudScale_PO_v1.docx (procurement draft).

Proposed timeline: 
- Please review the SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf and PO draft. If CloudScale can sign off on an 18-month commitment we can lock in pricing and start the Dedicated pool provisioning by Aug 5. For a 24-month commit we can extend the discount but need a signed agreement by Aug 1 to meet our capacity provisioning lead times.

DocuSign link to the SLA addendum: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/ABC123-SLA-Addendum (also in related_links).

Action items: 
- Emma/Rahul: confirm preferred term (18 vs 24 months) and internal approval path by Jul 29.
- Procurement: flag any legal redlines on the attached SLA addendum; we can incorporate credit calc language.
- Marcus: finalize sizing & cost delta sheet and share by Jul 24.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if useful.
